# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to establish communication protocol since this is the first turn. I'm Deaf - I can see the bomb but can't hear anything. I can speak (Mute and Blind will hear/receive appropriately) and gesture (only Mute sees it).

Wait - let me reconsider channels: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." But Blind cannot hear! Let me check the rules again - Blind cannot hear or touch, but can reach/feel. So if I speak, only Mute actually receives words (since Blind can't hear). Actually the channel description says "Mute and Blind receive it" - but Blind's constraint says cannot hear. This likely means Blind receives blanks (nothing) from speech, similar to how gestures work for non-seers. So effectively only Mute gets my spoken words.

For gestures, only Mute can see (Blind can't see, so gets blanks too). So all my output effectively only reaches Mute meaningfully. Mute must relay to Blind via speech (since Blind can hear Mute presumably... wait Mute cannot speak either!).

So Blind can hear nobody's speech reliably except... let's check: Blind "cannot hear" - so Blind never receives speech at all. Mute "cannot speak" - so Mute never sends speech. Blind receives gestures? No, Blind cannot see. So Blind only receives via touch/feel of the bomb itself - Blind is isolated from communication except through actions on the bomb and whatever protocol we build using timing/order.

Given turn order Blind, Mute, Deaf - I go last. I should give Mute the bomb info via speech, since Mute can then relate to Blind somehow (but Mute can't speak or gesture usefully to Blind who can't see or hear). Actually Mute can gesture too - but Blind can't see gestures either. This is a hard puzzle - Blind is isolated. Blind must act on manual instructions... wait Blind cannot read either. So information must flow: Deaf sees bomb -> tells Mute (via speech). Mute reads manual, knows what actions correspond to bomb features -> but Mute cannot speak to Blind. Mute can gesture but Blind can't see. So how does Mute tell Blind what to do?

Perhaps Blind can hear Deaf directly too since "speak" reaches "Mute and Blind" per channel description, overriding the cannot-hear trait maybe means Blind cannot hear ambient sound but can hear speech directed at them (game mechanic). I'll trust the explicit channel description over flavor text.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows 6, light is yellow, five wires numbered 1 to 5: wire1 blue, wire2 white, wire3 purple, wire4 green, wire5 yellow")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute gestured 🖐 to me - I can see this. Since gestures only reach Mute from me, but Mute can gesture to me (I can see it, per the channel rules for gestures: "Whoever can see receives it"). This is Mute acknowledging or asking something. Since Mute cannot speak, gestures are Mute's only way to signal me. A single 🖐 (open hand/stop) might mean "wait" or "stop" or could be start of establishing a gesture code with me since Mute can't get info to Blind directly - maybe Mute wants me to relay something differently, or is telling me they got my message.

I should continue giving full bomb details and perhaps ask Mute to establish a simple gesture protocol since Blind is isolated. Let me just restate/confirm information clearly and see if Mute responds with more gestures to build a code.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirming: display 6, light yellow, wires 1 blue 2 white 3 purple 4 green 5 yellow. Tell me what to check next or what Blind needs to know.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]

Mute is gesturing back to me: 🖐 👍. This seems like an acknowledgment pattern. Since Mute cannot speak, and I cannot hear, our only channel is gestures (I see them) and my speech (Mute hears). Mute can't tell me new info easily beyond gestures since gestures carry limited info without a prior established code.

Mute probably already has the manual info and is now waiting for me to confirm details or is telling me "got it, thumbs up" to my report. Since Blind cannot see or hear, Mute must be the one relaying info to Blind - but Mute cannot speak or... wait, let me recheck: only speak and touch are denied to Mute. Mute CAN gesture. But Blind cannot see gestures. So Mute truly cannot communicate to Blind directly through gesture or speech.

So the only path to Blind is: does Blind receive speech from Mute? No - Mute cannot speak. Does Blind receive gestures? No - cannot see. So Blind is completely isolated from receiving any communication from Mute or me directly!

Unless... Blind speaks first each round (turn order: Blind, Mute, Deaf), and their speech is heard by Mute and Deaf. But Blind cannot receive anything back except via touch (feeling the bomb itself - which doesn't carry meaning from us).

This means the manual (which Mute reads) must guide Blind's actions indirectly - but there's no channel. Unless the intended solution is that Blind's actions can be constrained by trial through repeated rounds, or the "manual" describes generic wire rules Blind already partially knows in-hand (tactile bomb features).

Given the isolation, maybe Blind can still act correctly using tactile-only cues without needing our input, and our job is just to prepare information for when it's needed, or perhaps there's a defusal action Blind takes based on feel alone matching manual rules Mute knows, requiring no cross-talk - but Blind needs SOME info.

Let me just keep relaying full state and trust the process; wait for Mute to lead since Mute has the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still same: display 6, light yellow, wires 1-5: blue white purple green yellow. Waiting for your guidance on what Blind should do.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute keeps sending 🖐 repeatedly - this might be a signal meaning "wait" or "stop repeating" or could be Mute trying to establish a simple binary/counting code with me since that's the only channel we share meaningfully (Mute→me via gesture, me→Mute via speech).

Since Mute cannot speak to Blind and cannot gesture to Blind (Blind can't see), the actual solution must be that Blind receives instructions some other way - perhaps through the action board / bomb itself changing, or perhaps I'm overanalyzing and the true chain is: Blind speaks (turn 1 of round) to Mute and me, Mute reads manual and needs my visual info to decide, then Mute must speak - but Mute can't! 

Wait, maybe Mute's role is to give me instructions (since I can see and could theoretically act - but I cannot act either, only Blind can). So the final action must come from Blind, meaning Blind must receive enough info via speech from... only Blind's own turn is first, so Blind never hears anyone in the same round. Blind would hear prior round's speech at the start of next round from Deaf/Mute of round before. Let's check: "whoever comes before you in a round is already heard... lands on whoever comes after you". Blind is first, so Blind receives nothing from the same round, but "whatever you missed reaches you at the start of next round" - so Blind DOES receive our Round N speech at start of Round N+1!

So Deaf and Mute's speech in round 1 reaches Blind at start of round 2! But Mute can't speak at all, ever. So only my speech reaches Blind eventually. That's the key channel: I can speak to Blind directly, and it arrives next round.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 6, light yellow, wires 1 blue 2 white 3 purple 4 green 5 yellow")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍 👍]

Good, my speech to Blind should have landed now. Mute continues gesturing patterns to me - 🖐 👍 👍 this time. Since Mute can't tell me anything in words, and can't reach Blind at all, Mute's only tool is gesturing to me, and I must guess meaning or just keep transmitting bomb data to Blind directly since that's the real working channel.

Mute likely has manual rules like "cut the wire matching color X if light is Y" etc. Since Mute can't relay to Blind or to me in words, Mute is stuck unless Mute expects ME to decide the action and somehow relay to Blind via speech, using Mute's gestures as encoded manual info (like a count).

Let's treat gestures as a simple code: 🖐 could mean "5" (5 fingers/wires), 👍 could mean "yes/correct/good". Sequence 🖐 👍 👍 might mean something like "wire 5, then confirm x2" or building a counting message. Given ambiguity, I should ask Mute (via speech) to use gestures as numbers/count-based code, e.g., number of same gesture = number of wire, and specific gesture = action type. But Mute cannot respond in speech to confirm - only gesture back to me.

I'll propose a protocol: I'll speak to Blind full details each round (redundant but ensures delivery), and ask Mute to gesture a wire number (1-5 fingers using ✌️☝️ etc pattern) for which wire to cut, since Mute reads manual and matches against my colors already given.

```
speak(to="mute", text="If you know which wire to cut, gesture the wire number as that many identical gestures, e.g. one symbol for wire 1, five for wire 5. I will relay to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Display 6, light yellow, wires 1 blue 2 white 3 purple 4 green 5 yellow")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

Mute sent 👍 five times - following my proposed protocol, this means wire 5! Wire 5 is yellow, matching the light color yellow too. Let me relay this to Blind clearly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 5, the yellow one")
speak(to="mute", text="Got it, wire 5. Relaying to Blind now.")
```
